title: Traps
summary: The trapezius is a large diamond from the skull down to the mid-back and out to the shoulders. The upper part lifts and rotates the shoulder blades; the middle and lower parts pull them back and down. Shrugs and carries build the upper traps; rows and Y-raises the rest.

what_it_is.overview: The app has two map regions: upper traps (neck slope to the shoulder) and mid/lower traps (the diamond between the shoulder blades). Weekly targets count the whole muscle.

heads.name: Upper traps
heads.origin: The base of the skull and the ligament along the back of the neck.
heads.insertion: The outer third of the collarbone.
heads.fiber_direction: Run down and out from the neck to the shoulder.

heads.name: Middle traps
heads.origin: The spines of the lowest neck and upper mid-back vertebrae (about C7 to T3).
heads.insertion: The top of the shoulder (acromion) and the spine of the shoulder blade.
heads.fiber_direction: Run straight out from the spine to the shoulder blade.

heads.name: Lower traps
heads.origin: The spines of the mid-back vertebrae (about T4 to T12).
heads.insertion: The inner end of the spine of the shoulder blade.
heads.fiber_direction: Run up and out from the spine to the shoulder blade.

what_it_does.action: Elevation (shrugging) and upward rotation of the shoulder blade.
what_it_does.detail: Upward rotation, with the lower traps and serratus, lets the arm go overhead.

what_it_does.action: Depression (pulling the shoulder blades down) and upward rotation.
what_it_does.detail: Active in Y-raises and when reaching overhead.

what_it_does.action: Helps tilt and turn the head; holds the shoulders up under heavy loads.
what_it_does.detail: Why carries and deadlifts work the upper traps hard.

synergists.name: Levator scapulae
synergists.role: Lifts the shoulder blade with the upper traps; not tracked.

synergists.name: Rhomboids
synergists.role: Retract the shoulder blades with the middle traps.

synergists.name: Serratus anterior
synergists.role: Rotates the shoulder blade upward with the upper and lower traps.

antagonists.name: Lats and pec minor
antagonists.role: Pull the shoulder girdle down, opposing the upper traps.

antagonists.name: Serratus anterior (for the middle traps)
antagonists.role: Pulls the shoulder blades forward, opposing retraction.

stabilizer_roles.text: In deadlifts and carries the upper traps hold the shoulders against a heavy load without much movement; the library credits deadlifts 0.6 and farmer carries 0.8.
In overhead pressing the traps rotate the shoulder blades upward; the overhead press is rated 0.3.

relationships.indirect_note: Each working set adds the exercise's rating for this muscle to the weekly total, and ratings under 0.25 count as 0. 3 sets of barbell shrug (1.0), 3 sets of deadlift (0.6) and 4 sets of chest-supported row (0.5) give 3 + 1.8 + 2 = 6.8, which the panel shows as 7 (rounded to the nearest 0.5). The full list comes live from exercises.json; the rows above are examples and the ratings are coaching estimates.

how.joint_angle: Shoulders lifted straight up toward the ears.
how.stretch_position: Let the shoulders sink fully at the bottom.
how.grip: Dumbbells at the sides or a bar in front.

bias.caveat: Swaps that lose this show 'Less upper-trap work'. Straps help when grip limits the set.

how.joint_angle: Rows with the elbows out and a full squeeze of the shoulder blades.

bias.caveat: The library rates these rows 0.6 to 0.65 for traps, mostly mid/lower.

how.joint_angle: Arms raised in a Y overhead, shoulder blades pulled down and back.

bias.caveat: Light loads; the incline Y-raise is rated traps 1.0 with the mid/lower region at 1.0.
Removes the bar from the spine and the balance demand.

best_exercises.why: Heavy upper-trap isolation; loads progress easily.
Arms at the sides let the shoulders move straight up.
No spinal load and no grip-balance issue.
Upper traps 0.8 plus grip and trunk work.
Targets the lower and mid traps (traps 1.0).
Mid traps with the back; traps 0.6.
Very heavy upper-trap and back work; high fatigue and spinal load.

mistakes.text: Rolling the shoulders in circles on shrugs; it adds nothing and only the up-down part works.
Cutting shrugs short at the bottom.
Shrugging during rows and pulldowns when the goal is lats or mid-back.
Doing extra direct trap work when deadlifts, carries and rows already reach the target.

coach_cues.cue: Shoulders to ears, pause, all the way down.

coach_cues.why: Takes grip out as the limit.

notes: Weekly target in the app: 4 to 16 traps sets at Advanced. Intermediate and Beginner scale the minimum by 0.8 and 0.6; the maximum stays the same. Render the numbers from targets.json, not from this text.
No trap growth study by exercise choice is on file, so nothing here is marked supported.
Targets are low and marked extrapolated because pulls, carries and deadlifts give lots of indirect work.
